From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Ownership & commitment pathway — SLA, hosting mode, and procurement next steps

Hi Aaron / Lara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have a clear mutual action plan: 

1) Economic buyer and procurement
- Aaron confirmed he is the economic buyer and procurement loop will be Procurement@medisphere.io (copied above). They prefer a single-vendor contracting path and a 45-day procurement timeline.

2) Security & legal gating items
- You’ll send over the Medisphere security questionnaire (you said ~24–48h). We’ll respond and can provide SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, and optional on-prem packaging details.
- Data residency: you mentioned an EU patient dataset concern if we ingest EU PII. For initial pilot you prefer Hosted in us-west but may require Private (VPC) if PHI scope increases.

3) Decision criteria (what matters to your stakeholders)
- Latency: target p95 generation latency <= 200ms for single-turn API calls (embedding and sync generation).
- Cost: goal is to keep per-1000-token generation cost below $X (you gave a high-level target; need to confirm exact threshold).
- Reliability/SLA: procurement will ask for 99.9% uptime for production and a clear incident escalation flow.
- Deployment mode: short-term = Hosted API for speed of launch; medium-term = Dedicated GPU pool if throughput / data isolation require it.

Next steps / owners:
- Aaron: confirm final cost target (you said you’d check with finance) and procurement timeline.
- Lara: send the security questionnaire (attachment expected).
- Ben: can you pick up procurement coordination and draft a commercial summary (~1 page) + proposed SLA terms?
- Monica: please own the technical POC plan and perf test details (we need expected request profile and sample prompts).

Attachments: placeholder for Medisphere security questionnaire (if you prefer, send as PDF).

I’ll schedule a short call next week to review our response and agree on the pilot acceptance criteria.

Thanks —
Soojin

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: I’m the economic buyer and will own the final sign-off. My finance partner has set a rough internal bar around unit economics; I’ll aim to confirm the exact number by EOD Friday.
- Procurement: Procurement team prefers a concise commercial summary + SOW rather than a long contract up front. Net-30 is OK but will need final legal review.
- Security: attaching the initial security questionnaire (first pass) — it’s short but will be used to triage whether we need an NDA + onsite audit.
